sentences.text: 2. Second supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Mohd. Farooq, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Satyanand Tripathi, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.462 of 2024, under Sections 376, 342, 419, 506 I.P.C. and 3/5(1) of U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, Police Station-Khoda,
District-Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. This is the second bail application.

First bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 27.02.2025 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
45695 of 2024.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
45695 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 6. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have befriended the victim in the year 2024 as he was living in vicinity of her house and had established corporeal relationship with her without her consent after threatening her to commit the murder of her family members.

The applicant is even stated to have taken away the victim with her to Court on 19.03.2024 and made her to sign certain documents whereby she learnt about the religion of the applicant and she returned to her house but the said relationship continued under duress.
The applicant is stated to have taken her to Mumbai and continued the said relationship.
The applicant is even stated to have tried to convert her to his religion, as such, victim had given an application at the police station on 15.08.2024 7.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
FIR is delayed and there is no explanation to the said delay caused.
The victim has not raised any alarm whatsoever during his sojourn from Ghaziabad to Mumbai, as such, victim is consenting party.
The said allegation that applicant tried to convert her and concealed his religion is false.
8. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that statement of victim recorded under Section 183 BNSS is contrary to the FIR while the FIR was instituted by the victim herself.
The allegations have been escalated in the said statement recorded under Section 183 BNSS after legal consultation.
Applicant has criminal history of two cases in which he is already enlarged on bail.
The victim is major aged about 20 years.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 15.08.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty Sameer vs State Of U.P. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42330829/
2 of bail.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that applicant has concealed his religion and had given different addresses at different stages and there are four addresses of the applicant in all.
The statement of victim has been recorded in Court on 22.08.2025 and the cross-examination has been adjourned by the counsel for the applicant.

The applicant is at flight risk having criminal antecedents to his credit,
as such, applicant is not entitled for bail.
10.
This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.
As per the status report dated 06.08.2025 received from the trial court concerned no witness has been examined.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the delay in institution of FIR and the said inconsistency in the statement of victim to the FIR as also the period of incarceration of the applicant, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Sameer, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

14. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
